speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
text: asked the Minister for Social and Family Development whether the Ministry will consider a text messaging service in addition to the 24-hour National Anti-Violence Helpline to allow for the quick reporting of family violence cases or urgent queries for assistance via non-verbal means.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: These modes of reporting would enable persons to quickly provide necessary details, such as timing, location and other key observations of the violent incidents, for follow-up action through an easy-to-use form.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: These new modes of reporting will increase the accessibility of NAVH and make it easier for survivors and bystanders, including persons who are unable to call NAVH, to report violence discreetly.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: MSF will give some time for the changes to stabilise.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: NAVH should not be used for emergencies when there is imminent danger to safety.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: It is very welcoming news of the new modes of reporting and assistance to complement NAVH.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: With discreet text messages or through web link or through the app, we do need to consider two considerations.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: One, is to minimise the risk of interception of the chat history, data on iCloud, the conversation thread; second, is preventing impersonation, perhaps by the use of code words or a phrase.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: In other jurisdictions, they will use code words like S-A-F-E to convey that there is some unsafe access to the conversations.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Could MSF look into this while looking into the rolling out of the other modes of reporting, to look at how to further enhance the protection and perhaps in concert with colleagues from MCI as well, together with the recently announced Code of Practices on Social Media Platforms?

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I would appreciate any clarifications in that regard.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Indeed, the security of client data is very important to us.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: That is why we are not just purchasing off-the-shelf solutions.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: I mentioned earlier that we are looking into rolling out an easy-to-use form via a web link or a mobile application.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: That easy-to-use form would already include areas where the caller can include items, such as timing, location and other details, that will be helpful to allow first responders to reach the person who is asking for help.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: That is why we had the signal for help hand signal to help the vulnerable as well as children who are suffering, potentially, from abuse and neglect.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: This was something that the Member had suggested.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: MSF had taken it up and we rolled it out as part of our "Break the Silence" campaign.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We will continue to look into improving the different modes and channels in which survivors and potential victims can report.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Because the information is triaged out into the Family Violence Specialist Centres or the Family Service Centres, to ensure that callers not only have convenient and safe modes of reporting, but also, that they get the help that they need.
